tx-collin-2026-cad-p2-smith-michael.name: Michael G. Smith
tx-collin-2026-cad-p2-smith-michael.bio: Business executive and Certified Public Accountant with tax and governance experience.

positions.stance: Says property owners deserve accurate, consistent appraisals, efficient operations, clear explanations and professional treatment.
Expects transparent recruitment, objective criteria and eligibility and conflict checks for Appraisal Review Board members, who should be impartial.
Would ensure taxpayers are heard, the process is fair and transparent, protest rights are accessible and taxpayers receive due process.
Would focus the board on accurate appraisals amid rapid growth, cost control, measurable results, litigation trends, efficiency and taxpayer service.

source.label: their League of Women Voters of Collin County voters guide answers

tx-collin-2026-cad-p3-corcoran-joe.name: Joe Corcoran
tx-collin-2026-cad-p3-corcoran-joe.bio: Richardson City Council member (2021-2026) and chair of its audit committee.

positions.stance: Main initial goal is recruiting qualified Appraisal Review Board applicants, visiting chambers, trade, community and homeowner groups to assess needs.

source.label: their League of Women Voters of Collin County voters guide answers

tx-harris-2026-hcad-p1-blueford-daniels-.name: Kathy Blueford-Daniels
tx-harris-2026-hcad-p1-blueford-daniels-.bio: Harris Central Appraisal District director for four years and former HISD trustee.

positions.stance: Wants the guardrails set after the board selected a new HCAD chief appraiser in January 2026 continued, re-evaluated, improved or maintained.
Will pursue customer service improvements at HCAD and broaden community question-and-answer meetings.

source.label: their League of Women Voters Houston voter-guide answers

tx-harris-2026-hcad-p1-barrett-beverly.name: Beverly Barrett
tx-harris-2026-hcad-p1-barrett-beverly.bio: Business management professor at the University of Houston and former program director for Literacy Texas.

positions.stance: Will focus on modernization and on serving all residential and commercial property owners in Harris County.
Will bring a motion recommending a review of HCAD processes to ensure best practices in appraisals and appeals, with fair and transparent valuations.
"Earn the public's trust through open, ethical, and impartial governance."
"Deliver measurable results, responsible spending, and responsive taxpayer service."
Wants to bring a deep understanding of Harris County to appraisal accuracy.

source.label: their League of Women Voters Houston voter-guide answers

tx-harris-2026-hcad-p2-ehlinger-chris.name: Chris Ehlinger
tx-harris-2026-hcad-p2-ehlinger-chris.bio: Former commercial loan officer and manager with 25+ years in public accounting, banking and executive management.

positions.stance: In budget review, will watch how AI is integrated into HCAD and fund only the most appropriate uses so appraisals are fair and transparent.
Will use thorough interviews when appointing Appraisal Review Board members to keep the process free from political interference.

source.label: their League of Women Voters Houston voter-guide answers

tx-harris-2026-hcad-p2-wilson-jourdyn.name: Jourdyn Wilson
tx-harris-2026-hcad-p2-wilson-jourdyn.bio: Harris County property owner and self-described communicator, organizer and advocate.

positions.stance: Plans community workshops explaining how HCAD works.
Wants plain-language protest guides so neighbors don't need a tax firm or lawyer to protest.
Wants a renewed focus on making sure taxpayers feel heard throughout the review process.

source.label: their League of Women Voters Houston voter-guide answers

tx-harris-2026-hcad-p2-gutierrez-claudio.name: Claudio Gutierrez
tx-harris-2026-hcad-p2-gutierrez-claudio.bio: Business owner, project manager, consultant and ISO 9001 quality professional.

positions.stance: Will focus on appraisal methodologies, quality controls, performance measures and transparency to find and correct disparities between comparable properties.
Wants to reduce HCAD's operational expenses by identifying waste, streamlining processes and controlling costs.

source.label: their League of Women Voters Houston voter-guide answers

tx-harris-2026-hcad-p3-moses-cris.name: Cris Moses
tx-harris-2026-hcad-p3-moses-cris.bio: Pastor, community leader and real estate professional.

positions.stance: Will push for simpler notices, better online tools and stronger public communication on how values are set and how to protest.
Supports regular performance reviews, stronger quality control, staff training and responsible technology use to make appraisals fair and consistent.

source.label: their League of Women Voters Houston voter-guide answers

tx-harris-2026-hcad-p3-mccrutcheon-erick.name: Ericka McCrutcheon
tx-harris-2026-hcad-p3-mccrutcheon-erick.bio: Current Harris Central Appraisal District board member, business owner, licensed insurance agent and Realtor.

positions.stance: Says education and community engagement are top priorities so owners understand appraisals, exemptions and how to protest.
Supports investing in technology that makes appraisal information and resources easily accessible.
Wants to meet residents at churches, community centers and civic organizations so seniors and other taxpayers get guidance.

source.label: their League of Women Voters Houston voter-guide answers
